thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH severity — GPU pool 'gpu-prod-west' nearing capacity (98%). Autoscaler attempted scale but hit scale_limit. Queue growth observed on inference-queue-14. Prefix cache miss rate has spiked. Paging oncall.

maya: @incident-bot seeing the alert, I'm oncall. Confirming customer impact?

customer-success: Multiple customers reporting timeouts and 5xx spikes for completion routes. A couple of enterprise customers saw tail latency > 12s and error rates increased ~3x. Tickets coming in.

eli: Root cause initial read: continuous-batching rollout (was rolled 2h ago) introduced a smaller batch window + stricter prefix_cache_ttl which increased cache misses and reduced effective throughput. Autoscaler reacted to queue growth but couldn't provision due to per-pool scale_limit (we hit hot-shard throttling).

jon: Repro'd with load test: throughput down ~30% when prefix cache miss rate > 60%. We saw a backlog in the feeder queues and the autoscaler backoff kicked in due to failed handshakes to hotshards. Logs: ```kvcache: miss_rate=0.63 pref_lookup=0.17 eviction=high
autoscaler: attempted_scale=8 -> failed_reason=scale_limit_reached
runtime: batch_window_ms=22 -> tried_batch=64 -> actual_served=42```

maya: Immediate mitigation options? Prefer fixes that avoid customer-facing downtime.

eli: Mitigate plan A (fast): revert the continuous-batching rollout to previous config (rollback), and increase prefix_cache_ttl to previous value. This should reduce miss storm and restore throughput.

eli: Plan B (if rollback doesn't catch up quickly): temporarily bump pool scale_limit in prod-west (manual override) and add reserve capacity (hot spare) while we stabilize.

jon: Also recommend temporarily disable the new batching heuristic (set `batch_window_ms` to safe default 50ms) — that reduces partial batches and KV pressure.

deploy-bot: Release 2026.3.14-rc5 rollback initiated by @eli. Rolling back continuous-batching flags in config: `rb-continuous-batching=true -> false`. Target: 3 AZs in prod-west first, then expand.

sre-rotation: I'll take handoff for infra changes. @eli please post the exact terraform/patch commands and I'll apply. Also need to notify capacity ops for manual pool bump.

eli: Patch snippet (apply carefully):
```
# runtime config patch
PATCH /configs/continuous-batching
{"enabled": false, "batch_window_ms": 50, "prefix_cache_ttl_s": 900}

# scale limit bump (manual)
PATCH /pools/gpu-prod-west/policy
{"scale_limit": 24}
```
I will push the rollback to config-store now.

maya: I'll open a live incident bridge. @customer-success please keep me posted on new tickets and any customer escalation.

customer-success: On it — we've flagged top-3 affected customers and opened status page update draft. Expect a surge of messages once errors drop.

deploy-bot: Rollback to previous batching config completed in config-store (change-id: cs-2026-314-rollback). Rolling out to AZ a, b, c sequentially.

eli: After rollback started, prefix cache miss rate fell from 62% -> 18% on shard-3 within 90s. Queue drain rate improved but we still have backlog. Requesting manual scale_limit bump now.

sre-rotation: Scaling policy patched, bumping scale_limit -> 24 (applied). Manual hot spare allocation requested and provision triggered.

jon: Observability: token throughput back to ~92% of baseline, p99 latency dropping. Still seeing a few stalled feeders due to prefixed shard rebalances — working with runtime to drain them.

maya: Customer impact update?

customer-success: Error rate trending down. Two customers already reporting normal behavior. Status page published: "Intermittent increased latency and errors affecting text-generation routes in prod-west; mitigation in progress."

eli: Postmortem action items (initial):
- revert safe defaults to batching flags and add canary gating (no global rollout without perf gate)
- add autoscaler telemetry for "scale_limit_hit" as a first-class SLI and alert
- improve prefix cache canaries to detect miss-rate regressions before rollout
- docs: clearer runbook for manual scale_limit bump and hot spare allocation

jon: Added: add automated rollback if prefix_cache_miss_rate > 0.4 for >2m during rollout.

maya: Great. I'll keep this thread open during bridge. If anyone finds other customers impacted, ping here. Thanks all for fast response. :thumbsup:
